instruments.name: Provident funds
instruments.blurb: EPF and PPF. Steady, government-set returns, locked in until you retire.

provenance.basis: PPF has paid 7.1% since April 2020 (small-savings notices via secondary sources, rate reset quarterly). EPF 8.25% for FY2024-25 is from memory of the EPFO announcement and was not confirmed in this pass. 7.6% is a rough blend. Held constant across regimes because rates are set by the government.

instruments.name: Equity index funds
instruments.blurb: Shares through a low-cost index fund. High long-run growth, scary dips.

provenance.basis: Calibrated so the long-run mix gives about 14% average a year, 19% volatility and about 12.2% compounded. Anchor: Nifty 50 TRI 20-year CAGR of about 12.4% (secondary sources citing NSE data as of March 2026; not checked against NSE directly) and a calendar-2008 drawdown of roughly -60% on a TR basis (NSE whitepaper). The 19% volatility is an estimate; no 20-year figure was found.

instruments.name: Fixed deposits
instruments.blurb: Bank deposits. Safe and boring; barely beats inflation.

provenance.basis: Rough 5-year bank FD rates, falling when the economy slows. No current rate was confirmed in this pass (SBI's rate page was not found). Pre-tax.

instruments.name: Gold
instruments.blurb: India's favourite safety blanket. Tends to hold up when shares fall.

provenance.basis: Compounds at about 11% in the long-run mix. Secondary sources give rupee gold CAGRs of roughly 10-15% over 10 years and 8-15% over 20 years, with a large share from rupee weakness; 11% is a central pick. Volatility and the safe-haven pattern across regimes are estimates, not sourced.
Regime-dependent annual returns, drawn independently each year (no equity-gold correlation beyond the shared regime). All pre-tax and before fund costs; tax arrives in a later step.
